title: A Look at Hunted: Mining Colony 415
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5R6l50LDlV4

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at Hunted: Mining Colony 415 by Gabe Barrett, a small-box solo game that simulates the climactic final reels of Alien and Aliens: fight off the creatures, reach the launch pad before the colony self-destructs, and rescue your crew and your cat along the way. He expected something as simple as Chainsaw Warrior and found more crunch than that, with push-your-luck, light resource management and a dexterity mechanism he calls the perfect amount of spice.

Time is the main resource, ticking down from twenty as you shoot, hide or trigger rooms. Health governs the size of the token you flip, so wounded characters literally have a harder time landing shots. The location deck loses two random cards each game and hides the launch pad in the bottom three, and you must kill the queen before you can leave. Survivors from the Hunted deck give abilities: one unlocks doors, one lends three bullets, one hands over a grenade, and Sprinkles the cat grants re-flips. Bell icons track the noise you have made, so a second alien card can trigger an ambush unless you spend time to hide and clear the row. Tests and combat both come down to flicking tokens into a target box on an easy or hard side. Daniel has lost twice today and loves it, and is buying the Die Hard-flavoured entry in the same series next.

----

Hunted turns combat into flicking tokens into a box. Does a dexterity element add tension to a thematic solo game for you, or break the immersion?
